newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-UBS 9-month result up, Q3 lagged.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UBS 9-month result up, Q3 lagged.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), Switzerland's largest bank, on Monday said results for the first nine months of 1996 were higher than a year earlier but the third quarter lagged strong first-half results.

"As anticipated, third-quarter earnings at Union Bank of Switzerland did not prove as strong as in the first half of the year, due to the usual summer lull. Overall, however, operating results for the first nine months were good," UBS said.
In a statement which contained no absolute numbers, UBS said it remained positive for the outlook for the year as a whole. But it warned that final results would depend partly on provisions.

"The group's forecast for 1996 operating profit remains cautiously optimistic. Given the market situation, group earnings can be expected to remain good. The final result, however, will ultimately depend on provisioning requirements for credit risks in Switzerland," UBS said.
"Provisions for credit risks continued to be higher than expected," it added with respect to the nine-month results.
It said that cash flow and group profit were "not only higher than a year earlier but were also more than 75 percent of last year's full figure."
Trading income declined in the third quarter and was well below the level of the first two quarters, UBS said. But it added that cumulative growth for the first nine months of 1996 remained strong.
"At end-September trading income was already higher than last year's full figure," it said.

"The strongest contribution came from the equities sector. Trading in bonds and in interest rate instruments also continued its positive trend. Income from foreign exchange and banknote trading, however, was down versus a year earlier."

"Cumulated for the first nine months of this year, fees and commissions from securities and investment business together made a very pleasing contribution to income," it said, adding the contribution was also well up on the year-earlier level.
It said further recovery was noticeable in net interest income, which showed a slight year-on-year increase on a cumulative basis.

UBS reported a sharp 33 percent rise in net profits for the 1996 first half, with group net profit including minority interests at 1.109 billion francs ($880 million) compared with 836 million in the first half of 1995.
CS Research analyst Madeleine Hofmann said the latest results were mostly in line with expectations, although the continued high level of provisions was disappointing.

But, she said that high provisions were to be expected given the continued weakness in the Swiss economy, which along with depressed real estate prices has forced domestic banks to set more provisions for higher lending risks to corporate clients.
"In principle it is not surprising, when you look at the economy," Hofmann said. "While real estate remains a problem, it is now more a problem of small- and medium-sized companies."

Hofmann said she kept to her forecast for full-year 1996 profits of 2.006 billion francs versus 1.673 billion in 1995. She said CS continued to value UBS with a underweight rating. ($1 = 1.2650 Swiss francs)
